learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the brilliant minds of ancient Indian thinkers! Understand the core schools of Indian philosophy (Darshanas) and their logical quest for truth and liberation.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In India, philosophy is called 'Darshana', which literally means 'vision' or 'direct perception of truth'. It is not just intellectual thinking, but a practical way to achieve the ultimate goal of life: liberation from suffering.

Indian philosophy is divided into two broad categories based on whether they accept the authority of the Vedas. 'Astika' (Orthodox) schools accept the Vedas, while 'Nastika' (Heterodox) schools reject them.
These are Nyaya (Logic), Vaisheshika (Atomism), Samkhya (Dualism of matter and spirit), Yoga (Practical discipline), Mimamsa (Ritual philosophy), and Vedanta (Philosophy of the Upanishads).
The three major Heterodox schools are Buddhism, Jainism, and Charvaka. Charvaka is uniquely a completely materialistic school that believes only in what can be directly seen and touched.
How do we know what is true? Philosophers debate 'Pramanas'. The main ones are Pratyaksha (Direct Perception), Anumana (Inference/Logic), and Shabda (Verbal Testimony/Expert words).

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Smoke and Fire Logic
fun_activity.instructions: Look out the window and imagine seeing smoke rising from a distant hill. You immediately think, 'There must be a fire!' This is 'Anumana' (Inference), the core of the Nyaya school of logic. You deduced the unseen (fire) from the seen (smoke)!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define the difference between Astika (Orthodox) and Nastika (Heterodox) based ONLY on the acceptance of the Vedas, NOT on the belief in God.
📌 Memorize the names of the 6 Astika schools (Shad Darshana) as they are frequently asked.
📌 Know that the 'Charvaka' school is materialistic and accepts only 'Pratyaksha' (Direct Perception) as a valid source of knowledge.
quick_recap: ⭐ The ultimate goal of almost all Indian philosophical systems is Moksha (liberation from the cycle of birth and death).
⭐ Nyaya is famous for its sophisticated rules of logic and debate.
⭐ Vedanta is based on the Upanishads and focuses on the relationship between the individual soul (Atman) and universal reality (Brahman).
